designationHistory.indexText: Established Nov. 6, 2012, when the Fish and Wildlife Service accepted a donated 12-acre conservation easement from Openlands.

authority.citation: Acceptance of a donated 12-acre conservation easement (Openlands)

designationHistory.note: The refuge page does not say how it was established.

sources.name: U.S. Fish and Wildlife Service: Hackmatack National Wildlife Refuge, About Us
U.S. Department of the Interior press release, Aug. 15, 2012: Salazar authorizes establishment; refuge official only when first parcel acquired
FWS press release reprinted by McHenry County Blog, Jan. 13, 2013: approved July 10, 2012; first parcel (12-acre easement from Openlands) added Nov. 6, 2012

review.note: Date right, but this was an administrative action (Secretary Salazar authorized; FWS approved July 10, 2012). No presidential signature; clear Obama as signer.

designationHistory.indexOriginal: Hackmatack National Wildlife Refuge was established on November 6, 2012 with the donation of a 12 acre conservation easement conservation easement A conservation easement is a voluntary legal agreement between a landowner and a government agency or qualified conservation organization that restricts the type and amount of development that may take place on a property in the future.
